## The four configurations, side by side

| run | what was done | pitch found | pitch afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7-block fall with a water bucket | swept to **90.0** (the literal) | ~90 held at the goal |
| 2 | same fall, no bucket, maxFallHeightNoWater 10 | 85-89 through the fall | **90.0 held** at the goal |
| 3 | flat walk straight after run 2 | 88 at the start | 84-88 the whole walk, then ~90 for minutes |
| 4 | flat walk, rotation forced level first | 0 | **-4.1..+1.0 the whole walk** |
| 5 | mid-walk, pitch forced to 40 | 40 | 39.8-43.5 to the end of the walk and while idle |
| 6 | idle, pitch forced to 40 | 40 | **40.00 for 50 s** |


Reading: the pitch is stable around whatever value it currently holds, not around level.
Runs 4 and 6 are the control that shows the value is simply kept; runs 1-3 show what that means in
practice - a fall steepens the head and nothing brings it back up. This also reconciles the numbers
Nightjar measured (medians -9.5..7.4 after the fix): their walks started near level.
